description: Every dollar-denominated pure function this feature introduces (`computeLenderAvailableUsd`, `sumOutstandingPrincipalUsd`, `sumRecentGojoGiftsUsd`, `computeLoanCapUsd`, and REQ-104's `total_due_usd` formula) is specified as unclamped, plain floating-point arithmetic, and the spec's own Acceptance Criteria then demand EXACT-EQUALITY assertions against these unclamped results -- while never once adopting this SAME codebase's own already-established `.toFixed(6)` precision-clamping convention for money arithmetic, despite performing structurally identical floating-point operations (multiplication by a rate, exponentiation, chained subtraction) that convention exists specifically to protect. REQ-104 (line 455) specifies `total_due_usd = principal_usd * (1 + LOAN_INTEREST_RATE)` with no rounding step, and its own Acceptance Criteria (PROP-104a, verification-architecture.md line 92) demands this 'computes exactly `0.022` for `FIRST_LOAN_USD=0.02`' via 'unit test, fixed fixture, exact numeric assertion' -- i.e. a literal `===` comparison against unclamped floating-point multiplication output. Re-read this session, this EXACT codebase already has an established, adopted convention for precisely this hazard: `~/anicca/skills/economy/ubi/ubi.js::contribute()` (line 40) computes `const raw = +(totalRealizedProfitUsd * cfg.contributePct).toFixed(6);` and `~/anicca/skills/economy/gig/decide.mjs::decideGigAction()` (line 44) computes `const surplusUsdc = +(balanceUsdc - reserveUsdc).toFixed(6);` -- both explicitly re-coercing a floating-point dollar computation through `.toFixed(6)` before returning it, precisely because unclamped IEEE-754 arithmetic on decimal dollar amounts is unreliable for exact-equality comparisons (a well-known class of bug, the same one that makes `0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3` false in JavaScript). REQ-101's `computeLenderAvailableUsd`/`sumOutstandingPrincipalUsd`/`sumRecentGojoGiftsUsd`, REQ-105's `computeLoanCapUsd` (a doubling-ladder EXPONENTIATION of a non-power-of-two base, `0.02 * 2^n`), and REQ-104's `total_due_usd` (a rate multiplication) are all the SAME class of computation this codebase's own convention protects elsewhere -- yet none of their EARS text, Edge Cases, or Acceptance Criteria (verification-architecture.md PROP-101a/101d/104a/105a-b) mention or require this rounding step anywhere. An implementer following the formulas exactly as literally written, with no rounding, risks producing code that FAILS its own spec's stated exact-equality acceptance criteria due to floating-point representation drift -- and, more importantly for REQ-108's money-safety-relevant repayment-completion check ('value summed with prior partial repayments reaches at least total_due_usd'), an un-rounded `total_due_usd` with residual floating drift risks a loan that can never legitimately close (perpetually short by a sub-cent epsilon) or, depending on comparison direction, closes fractionally early.

evidence.snippet: total_due_usd = principal_usd * (1 + LOAN_INTEREST_RATE) -- simple interest, computed once at issuance, never recalculated.

crossCheck.note: This codebase's own established precision-clamping convention for dollar-arithmetic (also present at /Users/anicca/anicca/skills/economy/gig/decide.mjs line 44: `+(balanceUsdc - reserveUsdc).toFixed(6)`), never adopted or even mentioned anywhere in anicca-agent-lending's own money-arithmetic functions, despite verification-architecture.md's PROP-104a (line 92) requiring an exact numeric assertion against precisely this class of unclamped floating-point computation.
